Current H1: Evac+Chair 1-312 EVAC+Alarm Anti-Theft Alarm Device

Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 1-312 - EVAC+Alarm Anti-Theft Alarm Device
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair EVAC+Alarm is an anti-theft alarm device for an Evac+Chair evacuation chair or other building assets. It is fitted with a key-controlled alarm, and its battery-operated siren gives out an audible alarm when the chair is detached from its housing.
Evacuation chairs are kept in stairwells and corridors where anyone can reach them. This evacuation chair alarm discourages theft and misuse and lets people nearby know when the chair has been moved, so the chair is in place when it is needed. Its red face reads “STOP, Emergency Use Only” and “Alarm Sounds When Evac+Chair Is Removed,” so everyone can see the chair is protected.
Control: Key-controlled alarm
Siren: Battery-operated siren gives out an audible alarm when the evacuation chair is detached from its housing
Signage: Red STOP sign design marked “Emergency Use Only” and “Alarm Sounds When Evac+Chair Is Removed”
Use: Protects an Evac+Chair or other building assets
Available Models and Options
1-312 – EVAC+Alarm: Key-controlled anti-theft alarm device with a battery-operated siren
[H2] Applications
The EVAC+Alarm suits any building where an evacuation chair is kept in an open, public area.
Typical applications include:
Stairwells and corridors in offices, hotels, and high-rise buildings
Schools, universities, and public buildings
Hospitals, clinics, senior living, and care facilities
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
What does the EVAC+Alarm do?
It is an anti-theft alarm for evacuation chairs. When the Evac+Chair is detached from its housing, the battery-operated siren sounds, so people nearby know the chair has been moved.
Does the EVAC+Alarm lock the chair?
No. It is an alarm, not a lock. It sounds when the chair is detached from its housing, and it is controlled with a key.
Can it protect other equipment?
Yes. It can also protect other building assets, sounding when the asset is detached from its housing.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: as Ricky noted, "anti theft alarm" (100) is a broad term, so the H1 and meta title lead with the product name, and the keyword supports it: it is in the H1 (as part of the product name), first sentence, an FAQ answer, the meta title, and the meta description. "Evacuation chair alarm" is in the subtitle and second intro paragraph.
Specs: Evac+Chair publishes only one paragraph about this product and no data sheet (no battery type, sound level, size, or weight). A UK store (Safelincs) lists a 98 dB alarm and a reset key, but that is not from Evac+Chair, so I left it out. Do you have specs from Evac+Chair?
Mounting: Evac+Chair does not say how the alarm attaches to the chair or its wall bracket, so I did not describe it.
Name: Evac+Chair calls it the "Anti-Theft Alarm Device." I kept our name, EVAC+Alarm, and added "Anti-Theft Alarm Device" to the H1.
Signage: the wording on the device ("STOP, Emergency Use Only" and "Alarm Sounds When Evac+Chair Is Removed") is from the product photo.
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair text, plus an old "About Evac+Chair of North America" paragraph ending "Ask about their lifetime warranty." Evac+Chair gives no warranty for the alarm, so I left the warranty out. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: the one current image (1214×783) is the same as the only Evac+Chair photo. Evac+Chair has no other photos of it.
Weight: the variant is set to 4 lbs. Is that the real shipping weight?
Price: $140 with compare-at $187 (75%). No change made.
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
